newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cavallo's brother raided in Argentine graft probe.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo's brother raided in Argentine graft probe.

text.p: A police raid on offices of the brother of former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo turned up documents suggesting officials knew of the risk of graft in the customs service, a judge said Thursday.

A police crackdown last month revealed a major "parallel customs service" run by crooked officials that smuggled into Argentina goods worth about $10 billion, costing the state $3.0 billion in lost customs duties.

The man who was Cavallo's customs chief, Gustavo Parino, is under investigation and Federal Judge Guillermo Tiscornia said Wednesday's raid on Jorge Cavallo's consulting firm Latin Trade, in which no arrests were made, showed he sent Parino a detailed report in 1994 on the risk of customs graft.
Tiscornia told local radio it was a "structural analysis on the margins of risk in the structure of customs control."

The Radical Party deputy who started proceedings against Parino, Enrique Benedetti, said this would be "absolute proof that (Domingo) Cavallo and Parino knew for a fact about criminal activities, despite which they did nothing."

Benedetti and Tiscornia are bitter foes of Domingo Cavallo in his lone crusade against corruption. Since being sacked by President Carlos Menem in July, Cavallo has accused senior government officials of covering up bribery and corruption.
This Monday he accused Tiscornia of "judicial harassment" and of being "the principle protector" of smugglers.
Unlike other officials who are suing Cavallo, including Interior Minister Carlos Corach, Tiscornia shrugged off the allegations and said it was "not worth the effort" of fighting them.
